title: RAW UNREVIEWED: fixed interline ink-collision avoidance selects one-e placement
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A hand has a fixed preferred placement in each nominated single-e family. It switches only when a fixed alternate shape avoids pre-existing upper-line ink that the preferred shape would touch. No literal value or equivalence is established.

design.mechanism: For each nominated one-e pair, two fixed drawing templates of assumed equal advance width encode one hypothesized unnamed spelling cell. Use the hand preference unless preferred would collide with older upper-line ink and alternate would not; both free or both colliding use preference.
design.unit: A physically located complete one-e whole with predeclared templates and anchor; zero/two-e forms remain distinct and unmodified.
design.contrast: Same hand and family, both templates independently collision-free, versus a one-sided pre-existing-ink obstacle.
design.prediction: All both-free cases use the hand preference. Opposite placements in both-free cases of the same family/hand contradict the strict rule.
design.scope: Unassessed physical writing hypothesis, no actual geometry acquired, no historical attestation, meaning or global e normalization. Must independently specify templates, advance widths, placement anchors, already-written ink and boundary clearance before selection.

limitations: No claim that ASCII equality entails equal ink width.
Final whitespace is not independently available writing space.
Upper-line-first chronology is an assumption, not observed here.
GDT854 capacity stop stands and does not license a substitute classifier.
Root f77r pair supplied no positive geometry evidence.
Raw proposal retention is not novelty or scientific approval.
